decisions.reason: The date-control scope expansion does not necessarily change placeholder-clearing behavior; the source independently reports placeholder failures already represented by the candidate's same-message Events.
Extending calendar-based date functionality does not change the checklist-and-dropdown configuration.
The date-control scope expansion does not alter text wrapping or adjacent-column stability.
The source separately requests multiline support for the Board Seminar Item and Title field, but extending date functionality does not change that requirement.
The existing requirement already covers every interactive field; adding date controls to additional templates does not change its current rule or scope state.
The existing visual-cue rule already applies to interactive fields generally, and the source does not change how date fields must be visually identified.
The candidate concerns preserving Title-field formatting during interaction, which is unaffected by extending the reusable date control.
The architecture requirement already covers the template set broadly, and the source does not prescribe a new field implementation mechanism.
The Danish date-field placeholder remains valid for date fields generally; extending date functionality to more templates does not change the text or language rule.
Calendar date-control availability does not change hard-return spacing for continuous paragraph text.
Adding Board Seminar-style date functionality to the Board Meeting template does not change alignment of Item and Title.
The reusable date-control scope expansion does not alter Enter-key bullet creation behavior.
